In this case, the individual presented with a half-year history of pain in different parts of their body, and the pain gradually worsened, causing difficulty in walking and moving their shoulders."

We need see if claims support. C1: Stiff person syndrome symptoms usually develop over months to years and may remain stable for many years or slowly worsen. This establishes general symptom progression over months to years, slowly worsen. Could support "pain gradually worsened" maybe? But it doesn't mention half-year history, pain in different parts, difficulty walking and moving shoulders. It's generic disease symptom progression. Not substantive for specific case? C2: Stiff person syndrome may initially cause aching discomfort, stiffness, or pain, especially in lower back, hips, and/or legs; may also affect shoulders, arms, and/or neck, and progressive leg stiffness can lead to slow, stiff manner of walking. This supports pain in body parts, shoulders, difficulty walking? But not half-year history, not case report, not country. Parent requirement has two components: country condition and individual presentation. Claims are general about Stiff person syndrome. They don't mention the specific first case, country, half-year history. They are general disease symptoms. According to instructions, "general disease symptoms do not establish that a specific target patient had those symptoms." So likely no substantive support. But maybe C2 establishes material part: pain in different parts, difficulty walking and moving shoulders? However parent requirement is about a specific case. The claim is general. Does it "establish a material part of Parent Requirement with required entity, participant role, relation direction, object, temporal attachment, event/document binding, candidate branch." It lacks entity (specific individual), temporal attachment (half-year history), event binding (case reported). So not substantive.

Thus support_claim_ids: [] likely.
